# Introduction

The Palmer Penguins dataset was collected from three islands near Palmer Station, Antarctica:

- Biscoe
- Dream
- Torgersen

The dataset considers three species: Adelie, Gentoo and Chistranp, with observations from 2007 to 2009 (for Chinstrap only from 2007 to 2008). 



The data originates from [this article](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0090081).

![Penguin Species](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/refs/heads/main/man/figures/lter_penguins.png){width="70%"}

# Data Analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import os
sns.set_style("darkgrid")

penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins")

PATH = "/Users/jayballesteros/_github/uchicago-mpp/3_spring_2026/data_programming/skills-psets/_data"
penguin_years = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(PATH, "penguin_years.csv"))
penguins = penguins.join(penguin_years)

df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(PATH, "PalmerStation_Monthly_Weather.csv"), index_col='Date', parse_dates=True)
df["year"] = df.index.year
df_year = df.groupby("year")["Mean Temperature (C)"].mean()

penguins = penguins.merge(df_year, on="year", how="left")
penguins.rename(columns={"Mean Temperature (C)": "mean_temperature"}, inplace=True)
penguins['mean_temperature'] = penguins['mean_temperature'].round(2)
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

print(penguins.groupby("year")[["body_mass_g", 
"flipper_length_mm", 
"mean_temperature"]].mean().round(2))
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

print(penguins.groupby(["year", "species"])[["body_mass_g", 
"flipper_length_mm", 
"mean_temperature"]].mean().round(2))
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

sns.boxplot(data=penguins, x="year", y='body_mass_g', hue='species')
```

Across all three years, Gentoo penguins are consistently the heaviest species. Interestingly, 2009 has the highest average body mass and flipper length despite having the coldest temperature (-1.76°C), while 2008 was the warmest year (-0.78°C) but had lower averages. This suggests that annual mean temperature alone does not explain changes in penguin body size, and other factors likely play a wider role.
